ashok: Following up on the RFCI want to propose a post-ingest validation pipeline: keep a very small inline preflight (smoke + fingerprint) to unblock fastpath, but run a deeper, resumable compatibility harness asynchronously that validates a stratified sample and emits actionable findings.

marie: sounds pragmatic. do you plan a separate service or piggyback on the bench workers?

ashok: separate orchestration layer but reuse bench workers. controller submits jobs with runtime-profile matrix and collects granular results. advantage: minimal changes to intake RPCs, better fault isolation.

ben: main risk is late discovery. how do we prevent bad models from reaching prod customers?

ashok: two controls: 1) default: permissive deploy + shadow/canary routing (route a small percent for live verification). 2) opt-in strict policy flag per-organization that blocks full traffic until harness critical checks pass.

jia: harness reliability: we need checkpointing, idempotency, and reproducible failure bundles.

ashok: agreed. design: checkpoint cursor per-model-version, store artifact bundle (model ref, sampler-id, cursor, adapter-version), and attach reproducible-example snippets for each finding.

ben: about the sample: avoid massive corpora. propose a stratified mini-bench: 2k samples drawn across seqlen buckets, rare-token hits, and recent production signals. should be enough to catch most regressions while bounding cost (~2 GPUs x a few hours for large models).

marie: runtime mismatch is a common source of flakes. harness must run using the same runtime profile combinations (quantization, seq len, batch shapes) that we plan to serve.

ashok: harness will load runtime profiles from model metadata and try high-probability combos first (heuristics from traces). we iterate until coverage target reached or budget exhausted.

jia: adapter contract needs work. current adapter.verify() returns bool; propose adapter.check(model_ref) -> ordered findings with severity + reproducible example. e.g. [{"code":"IO_SHAPE","severity":"critical","example":"..."}].

ashok: yesharness will map critical findings to blocking behavior under strict policy, otherwise they surface as warnings and telemetry.

ben: telemetry: we need sample-level metrics tied to sample ids and probe ids so triage is fast. include runtime_profile, metric tags, and checksums.

ashok: plan: every harness envelope contains model_version, probe_id, input_id, runtime_profile, metrics (latency,p95,token_loss,hash). send to telem pipeline with dedup key and link to artifact bundle.

marie: who curates golden/sample sets? infra or product? small, representative sets need domain input.

ashok: infra provides the tooling and sampler primitives, product/vertical teams can register curated augmentations or customer-specific probes. infra owns drift detection and default samplers.

jia: UX/API: POST /models/:v/harness -> returns job_id + ETA; GET /harness/:job_id streams findings. include fastfail param for critical-only runs.

ashok: also add a CLI for partners: `ri harness run --samples 500 --fastfail` that wraps the POST and tailing.

ben: reuse bench-orchestrator to avoid duplication: submit `mini-bench` jobs with metadata and collect results. store run summary in model-registry (pass/fail, coverage_score, last_run_ts).

bench-bot: note: bench-orchestrator quotas apply. queues: bench-prod-1 cap=8, bench-prod-2 cap=4. coordinate large runs with infra.

marie: action items: ashok draft RFC v2 with adapter contract + job API; ben prototype sampler + perf/cost estimate; jia mock endpoints + streaming logs. sync next Wed.

ashok: I'll draft and tag @infra and @security for artifact policies. will post link here when ready. thanks! :thumbsup:
